exam_set.title: Practice Set 1
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 3, Practice Set 1

questions.jp: A、B、C、Dの順に到着するデータに対して、一つのスタックだけを用いて出力可能なデータ列はどれか。
questions.romaji: A, B, C, D no jun ni tōchaku suru dēta ni taishite, hitotsu no sutakku dake o mochiite shutsuryoku kanō na dēta retsu wa dore ka.
questions.en: For data arriving A, B, C, D in that order, which output sequence is possible using only one stack?

options.label: ア
options.romaji: A, D, B, C

options.label: イ
options.romaji: B, D, A, C

options.label: ウ
options.romaji: C, B, D, A

options.label: エ
options.romaji: D, C, A, B

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A stack works like a pile of plates: you can place a new plate on top, and you can remove only the plate currently on top. The data arrives in the fixed order A, B, C, D, so we may push each item only when it arrives. We cannot reach through the stack to remove an item underneath another item.

Technical breakdown:
Use the valid sequence step by step, with the right side as the top:
push A → [A]
push B → [A, B]
push C → [A, B, C]
pop → C, leaving [A, B]
pop → B, leaving [A]
push D → [A, D]
pop → D, leaving [A]
pop → A, leaving []
The output is therefore C → B → D → A. Every pop removes the current top, so this sequence obeys LIFO.

Japanese keywords to remember:
スタック = sutakku = stack
後入れ先出し = atoire sakidashi = last in, first out
プッシュ = pusshu = push
ポップ = poppu = pop

Why the best solution works:
The sequence C, B, D, A is possible because C and B are popped before D arrives, then D is pushed above A and popped, and A is removed last. No step requires removing an item buried under another item.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
After outputting A first, B and C arrive before D. To output D next, D is popped, but then C is above B, so B cannot be output before C.

イ:
Output B is possible after pushing A and B. But after D is output, C remains above A, so A cannot be output before C.

エ:
Push A, B, C, D and pop D then C. The remaining stack is [A, B], with B on top, so A cannot be output before B.

Memory trick:
For a stack, draw the stack after every push or pop. If an option asks for an item below the current top, that option is impossible.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: 待ち行列に対する操作を、次のとおり定義する。ENQ n：待ち行列にデータnを挿入する。DEQ：待ち行列からデータを取り出す。空の待ち行列に対し、ENQ 1、ENQ 2、ENQ 3、DEQ、ENQ 4、ENQ 5、DEQ、ENQ 6、DEQ、DEQの操作を行った。次にDEQ操作を行ったとき、取り出されるデータはどれか。
questions.romaji: Machigyōretsu ni taisuru sōsa o, tsugi no tōri teigi suru. ENQ n: machigyōretsu ni dēta n o sōnyū suru. DEQ: machigyōretsu kara dēta o toridasu. Sora no machigyōretsu ni taishi, ENQ 1, ENQ 2, ENQ 3, DEQ, ENQ 4, ENQ 5, DEQ, ENQ 6, DEQ, DEQ no sōsa o okonatta. Tsugi ni DEQ sōsa o okonatta toki, toridasareru dēta wa dore ka.
questions.en: Queue operations are ENQ n, insert n, and DEQ, remove data. After the listed operations on an empty queue, what does the next DEQ remove?

options.label: ア
options.romaji: ichi

options.label: イ
options.romaji: ni

options.label: ウ
options.romaji: go

options.label: エ
options.romaji: roku

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A queue is like people waiting in a checkout line. New people join at the back, and the person who has waited longest leaves from the front. ENQ adds an item to the back; DEQ removes the item at the front. Track the line after every operation rather than trying to remember it mentally.

Technical breakdown:
start []
ENQ 1 → [1]
ENQ 2 → [1, 2]
ENQ 3 → [1, 2, 3]
DEQ → 1, leaving [2, 3]
ENQ 4 → [2, 3, 4]
ENQ 5 → [2, 3, 4, 5]
DEQ → 2, leaving [3, 4, 5]
ENQ 6 → [3, 4, 5, 6]
DEQ → 3, leaving [4, 5, 6]
DEQ → 4, leaving [5, 6]
The next DEQ removes the front item, 5.

Japanese keywords to remember:
待ち行列 = machigyōretsu = queue
先入れ先出し = sakiire sakidashi = first in, first out
挿入 = sōnyū = insertion
取り出す = toridasu = remove

Why the best solution works:
After all listed operations, 5 has been waiting longer than 6 and is at the front of [5, 6]. FIFO therefore makes 5 the next value removed.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
1 was the first item removed by the first DEQ, so it is no longer in the queue.

イ:
2 was removed by the second DEQ, so it also cannot be returned by the next operation.

エ:
6 is still in the queue, but it was enqueued after 5. It is behind 5 and will be removed one DEQ later.

Memory trick:
Queue = a real waiting line: add at the back, remove at the front.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: データ構造の一つであるリストは、配列を用いて実現する場合と、ポインタを用いて実現する場合とがある。配列を用いて実現する場合の特徴はどれか。ここで、配列を用いたリストは、配列に要素を連続して格納することによって構成し、ポインタを用いたリストは、要素から次の要素へポインタで連結することによって構成するものとする。
questions.romaji: Dēta kōzō no hitotsu de aru risuto wa, hairē o mochiite jitsugen suru baai to, pointa o mochiite jitsugen suru baai to ga aru. Hairē o mochiite jitsugen suru baai no tokuchō wa dore ka.
questions.en: A list can use an array or pointers. Which is a feature of an array-based list?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 位置を指定して、任意のデータに直接アクセスすることができる。
options.romaji: Ichi o shitei shite, nin'i no dēta ni chokusetsu akusesu suru koto ga dekiru.
options.en: You can directly access any data by specifying its position.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 並んでいるデータの先頭に任意のデータを効率的に挿入することができる。
options.romaji: Narande iru dēta no sentō ni nin'i no dēta o kōritsuteki ni sōnyū suru koto ga dekiru.
options.en: You can efficiently insert arbitrary data at the front.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 任意のデータの参照は効率的ではないが、削除や挿入の操作を効率的に行える。
options.romaji: Nin'i no dēta no sanshō wa kōritsuteki de wa nai ga, sakujo ya sōnyū no sōsa o kōritsuteki ni okonaeru.
options.en: Arbitrary access is inefficient, but deletion and insertion are efficient.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 任意のデータを別の位置に移動する場合、隣接するデータを移動せずにできる。
options.romaji: Nin'i no dēta o betsu no ichi ni idō suru baai, rinsetsu suru dēta o idō sezu ni dekiru.
options.en: You can move data without moving adjacent data.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
An array is like a row of numbered lockers placed next to each other. If you want locker 20, you can calculate its location and open it directly. A linked list is more like a treasure hunt: each note tells you where the next note is, so reaching the twentieth item means following earlier links first.

Technical breakdown:
An array-based list stores elements in contiguous memory positions. Because each element has a fixed-size indexed position, the address of element i can be calculated directly, giving efficient random access. However, inserting or deleting near the beginning can require shifting many later elements. A linked list stores nodes connected by pointers; arbitrary access requires following pointers, but insertion or deletion can be efficient after the target position is found.

Japanese keywords to remember:
配列 = hairē = array
連続して格納 = renzoku shite kakunō = store contiguously
直接アクセス = chokusetsu akusesu = direct access
ポインタ = pointa = pointer

Why the best solution works:
Specifying an index lets an array calculate the desired element's address without visiting preceding elements. That is exactly the direct-access property described in ア.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Inserting at the front of an array normally requires shifting existing elements one position, so it is not generally efficient.

ウ:
This describes a linked list: arbitrary reference requires traversal, while pointer changes can make insertion and deletion efficient.

エ:
Moving an array element to another position normally requires shifting neighboring elements to keep storage contiguous. A linked structure can reconnect pointers instead.

Memory trick:
Array = numbered address, fast jump. Linked list = pointer chain, step-by-step walk.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: 配列と比較した場合の連結リストの特徴に関する記述として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Hairē to hikaku shita baai no renketsu risuto no tokuchō ni kansuru kijutsu to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Compared with an array, which statement about a linked list is appropriate?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 要素を更新する場合、ポインタを順番にたどるだけなので、処理時間は短い。
options.romaji: Yōso o kōshin suru baai, pointa o junban ni tadoru dake na node, shori jikan wa mijikai.
options.en: Updating is quick because pointers are only followed in order.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 要素を削除する場合、削除した要素から後ろのすべての要素を前に移動するので、処理時間は長い。
options.romaji: Yōso o sakujo suru baai, sakujo shita yōso kara ushiro no subete no yōso o mae ni idō suru node, shori jikan wa nagai.
options.en: Deleting takes long because all later elements move forward.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 要素を参照する場合、ランダムにアクセスできるので、処理時間は短い。
options.romaji: Yōso o sanshō suru baai, randamu ni akusesu dekiru node, shori jikan wa mijikai.
options.en: Referencing is quick because random access is possible.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 要素を挿入する場合、数個のポインタを書き換えるだけなので、処理時間は短い。
options.romaji: Yōso o sōnyū suru baai, sūkō no pointa o kakikaeru dake na node, shori jikan wa mijikai.
options.en: Insertion is quick because only a few pointers are rewritten.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Imagine train cars connected by couplers. To insert a new car, disconnect one link and connect the new car between its neighbors. A linked list works similarly with pointers. An array is more like assigned seats in one row: inserting a seat in the middle may force many people to move.

Technical breakdown:
A linked-list node contains data and a pointer to another node. Once the insertion position is known, insertion changes only a small number of neighboring pointers. An array keeps elements contiguous, so insertion in the middle may require shifting every later element. Pointers do not create random access: to reach an arbitrary node, the program still follows links from the start unless it already has that node's address.

Japanese keywords to remember:
連結リスト = renketsu risuto = linked list
要素 = yōso = element
挿入 = sōnyū = insertion
書き換える = kakikaeru = rewrite

Why the best solution works:
エ identifies the defining insertion advantage of linked lists: reconnecting a few pointers instead of shifting a long block of elements.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Following pointers in order is traversal, and reaching a distant element can take many steps. It does not automatically make updates fast.

イ:
Shifting all later elements is typical array behavior. A linked list deletes a known node by reconnecting neighboring pointers.

ウ:
Linked lists do not support array-style random access. A pointer leads only to the next node, so arbitrary access requires traversal.

Memory trick:
Array insertion shifts data; linked-list insertion switches links.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: 図の木構造は2分探索木である。a〜gの値の大小関係として、適切なものはどれか。ここで、a〜gの値は重複しないものとする。
questions.romaji: Zu no ki kōzō wa nibun tansaku-ki de aru. a kara g no atai no daishō kankei to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: The tree is a binary search tree. Which ordering of a through g is appropriate? Values do not repeat.

options.label: ア
options.romaji: a yori b yori d yori e yori c yori f yori g
options.en: a < b < d < e < c < f < g

options.label: イ
options.romaji: d yori b yori e yori a yori f yori c yori g
options.en: d < b < e < a < f < c < g

options.label: ウ
options.romaji: d yori e yori f yori g yori b yori c yori a
options.en: d < e < f < g < b < c < a

options.label: エ
options.romaji: g yori f yori c yori e yori d yori b yori a
options.en: g < f < c < e < d < b < a

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A binary search tree is an organized family tree of values. Every value smaller than a node goes somewhere in its left subtree, and every larger value goes in its right subtree. Reading left branch, then node, then right branch lists the values from smallest to largest.

Technical breakdown:
At root a, the left subtree contains b, d, e, so all are less than a. Within that subtree, d < b < e. The right subtree contains c, f, g, so all are greater than a. Within it, f < c < g. An in-order traversal visits left → root → right:
d → b → e → a → f → c → g.
For a BST with distinct values, this traversal is sorted, so d < b < e < a < f < c < g.

Japanese keywords to remember:
2分探索木 = nibun tansaku-ki = binary search tree
左部分木 = hidari bubun-ki = left subtree
右部分木 = migi bubun-ki = right subtree
重複しない = chōfuku shinai = no duplicates

Why the best solution works:
イ exactly matches the sorted order produced by the tree's in-order traversal and satisfies every parent-child relationship.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
It claims a < b, but b is in a's left subtree, so b must be less than a.

ウ:
It places a as the largest value, but c, f, and g are in a's right subtree and must all be greater than a.

エ:
It reverses several relationships; for example g is c's right child, so g must be greater than c, not less.

Memory trick:
BST exam shortcut: write left → root → right. The resulting list must increase.

Correct answer: イ
